enhanced.fullText:
The Higher Education Act's Program Participation Agreement disclosure requirements under 20 U.S.C. § 1094(a)(26) mandate that participating institutions provide disciplinary proceeding outcomes to victims of violent crimes and non-forcible sex offenses upon request. This provision establishes critical transparency obligations that complement broader campus safety requirements under the Jeanne Clery Disclosure of Campus Security Policy and Campus Crime Statistics Act (20 U.S.C. § 1092(f)).

Under this statutory framework, institutions must disclose the final results of institutional disciplinary proceedings conducted against alleged perpetrators when requested by the alleged victim. The disclosure obligation extends to next of kin if the alleged victim dies as a result of the crime or offense. This requirement applies to all Title IV-eligible institutions that have entered into Program Participation Agreements with the Department of Education.

The Violence Against Women Reauthorization Act of 2013 significantly expanded these disclosure obligations through amendments to 20 U.S.C. § 1092(f)(6)(B)(iv)(III), requiring simultaneous written notification to both accusers and accused parties regarding outcomes of disciplinary proceedings arising from domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, or stalking allegations. This dual notification requirement ensures procedural fairness while maintaining victim rights.

Institutions must establish clear policies defining "final results" to include sanctions imposed and rationale for the decision, as specified in 34 CFR § 668.46(b)(11). The disclosure must be provided regardless of whether the institution found the alleged perpetrator responsible for the violation. Privacy protections under FERPA (20 U.S.C. § 1232g) do not prohibit these required disclosures, as educational records may be disclosed to alleged victims of crimes of violence or non-forcible sex offenses.

Enforcement mechanisms include Program Participation Agreement violations, which may result in fine imposition, limitation or suspension of Title IV program participation, or termination proceedings under 34 CFR Part 668, Subpart G. The Department of Education monitors compliance through program reviews and complaint investigations. Recent guidance emphasizes that institutions must provide disclosures promptly upon request and maintain documentation of all disclosure activities for audit purposes.

Non-compliance can result in significant financial penalties, loss of federal funding eligibility, and potential civil liability under Title IX. Institutions must integrate these requirements into comprehensive campus safety policies that address both criminal and disciplinary proceedings while ensuring coordination between campus security, student affairs, and legal counsel.
enhanced.summary: Higher education institutions must disclose disciplinary proceeding outcomes to victims of violent crimes and non-forcible sex offenses upon request, with simultaneous notification required for VAWA-covered offenses under 20 U.S.C. § 1094(a)(26).
enhanced.requirements:
## Core Disclosure Obligations
- Provide final disciplinary proceeding results to alleged victims upon written request per 20 U.S.C. § 1094(a)(26)
- Include sanctions imposed and decision rationale in all disclosures
- Notify next of kin if alleged victim dies as result of the crime

## VAWA Notification Requirements
- Simultaneously notify both accuser and accused parties in writing for domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, and stalking cases
- Ensure notifications occur within reasonable timeframe after disciplinary decision
- Document all notification activities for compliance verification

## Policy Development
- Establish written procedures defining "final results" and disclosure processes
- Train designated personnel on disclosure obligations and FERPA exceptions
- Coordinate with Title IX office and campus security personnel

## Documentation Standards
- Maintain records of all victim requests and institutional responses
- Document disclosure timing and delivery methods
- Preserve files for Department of Education program review purposes
enhanced.reportingRequirements: No specific federal reporting deadlines apply; however, institutions must respond promptly to victim requests and maintain disclosure documentation for Department of Education program reviews and compliance audits.
